22.t: Working with data: catalase at four temperatures
q: Calculate the initial rate at 45 °C (first 10 s). Give the units.
At 45 °C the reaction starts fastest, but less oxygen is made in total than at 35 °C. Explain.

At 45 °C molecules have more kinetic energy, so there are more successful collisions at first. But the enzyme is slowly denaturing, so the reaction stops before the substrate is used up. At 35 °C the enzyme stays active.
A student says the optimum temperature of catalase is 45 °C. Evaluate this conclusion.
True for the initial rate, but over 60 s, 35 °C gives more product. The answer depends on how long the reaction runs, and no temperatures between 35 and 45 °C were tested.
Explain why the 60 °C curve levels off at 1.2 cm³.
The enzyme is fully denatured within about 30 s, so the reaction stops even though plenty of hydrogen peroxide is left.
Predict the total volume of oxygen at 20 °C if the reaction runs for 10 minutes. Explain.
About the same as the final volume at 35 °C (about 10 to 11 cm³): the same amount of substrate gives the same amount of product, just more slowly, because the enzyme stays active at 20 °C.
